title: Sirena Tuna varieties 95g $1.98, 185g $3.09, 425g $5.10 @ Coles on Uber Eats
body:
Deal: Sirena Tuna varieties 95g $1.98, 185g $3.09, 425g $5.10 @ Coles on Uber Eats

[Bellpop] FWIW the Aldi yellowfin pole caught tuna is < $150/can from memory and just as good. Doesn’t really go off so can buy a whole slab.
[M00Cow] you reckon it tastes as good? I think not.
[ATTS] Whats your opinion john west? Its the main brand i eat for some reason
[M00Cow] terrible, I.suspect homebrand cans come.from there.
[ATTS] @M00Cow: Thanks i might try sirena again
[bobvegas] it's the lowest quality name brand. John West Tuna when it just says Tuna is the fishy tasting/smelling tuna, the cheap quality non Yellow FIn one. You can get John West Yellow Fin Tuna too, but it's normally twice the price of Woolworths Yellow fin, Woolworths brand is 75% Yellow Fin which is about as high as it gets. It looks and tastes the same.
Oh btw Yellow Fin although regarded as higher quality has a milder taste/smell, it's not fishy, but for someone that like fishy tuna, it is possible you'd not like Yellow fin.
[Charity] The reason is that you are extremely susceptible to TV programming and probably lack any meaningful critical thinking skills. By the way, John West. The Best. lol
[Shaun Prawn] I agree. But the Aldi one is pretty damn good for the price. It's is my second favourite to Sirena. While Sirena is the best in my opinion, at full price I think the Aldi one is the better buy, especially if you eat Tuna every day like I do.
[SometimesStingy] I recently found out that yellowfin shouldn’t be eaten everyday. I was doing this until I learned about the high mercury content. It’s the sad reality :(
[M00Cow] @SometimesStingy: yeah but is it actually a scientific-evidence based claim or.scaremongering on the internet?
https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-03-24/canned-tuna-safe-merc…
But how many tins a week?
Lab tests we did for the ABC TV science program Catalyst in 2015 suggest — depending on your body weight and the exact brand of tuna you buy — you could eat anywhere between 25 and 35 small tins (95g each) of tuna a week before you hit maximum mercury limits.
of course are you really eating 1 tin per day for months anyway?
[cloudy] @M00Cow: I actually met someone who felt the effects off mercury from too much tuna, and he was not going 25 tins a week.
I wouldn’t go more than a few cans a week. Having a more balanced diet in general is a good thing anyway
[M00Cow] @cloudy: you met someone who said they did. Doesn't mean it actually did. I have a neighbour who says the microwave oven gave their wife leukaemia.
They may have had elevated mercury levels, but it unlikely came from canned tuna. Because as the actual scientific evidence shows they'd need to eat over 3 can per day week in, week out.
[bargainshooter] @M00Cow: That's just rubbish - methylmercury accumulates. There's enough evidence it affects cognitive function esp in growing brains (children) and no level has been identified as safe. But is there a limit authorities recommend vs any potential reduction in profit?
[Shaun Prawn] @SometimesStingy: I have heard the same thing from multiple people over the years. I've been eating tuna every day at work (so only 5 days a week max) for more than 15 years. At the moment I'm only eating one tin each work day, but for many many years I was eating two tins per day. I haven't had my mercury levels checked specifically (not sure if general blood tests check mercury levels), but I definitely don't have any signs of mercury poisoning. Maybe I can ask the doc if it can be checked when I get my next blood test.
[SometimesStingy] @Shaun Prawn: That’s reassuring! I might be back on the tins 🥳
Keep me updated if you remember with the test. Also let me know if you start showing signs of growing a yellow fin.
[garage sale] Asking isn’t as good as Sirena but it’s better than John west and many of the others I Coles which are mainly skipjack. I tend to use Sirena for special occasions rather than the easy lunch box filler, that ones aldi.
[carrawa] Tastes fine. Most varieties have added taste. Preference.
Cracked pepper and lemon was good but the price kept going up and up.
[Gold3npanda] It's acceptable and much better than john west, but it's definitely not the same quality as Sirena.
Sirena has dropped slightly in quality since switching from olive oil to a mix of olive and veg oil, but it's still very good quality
[LiamD] The concept of ordering canned tuna on Uber eats
[Jimothy Wongingtons] If yall like tinned fish, I dare you to try the $4.99 Aldi smoked rainbow trout (not the truffle one) on a piece of sour dough and cream cheese and tell me it doesn’t touch your soul.
[AussieDaddy] The 110gm one in the tin (OceanRise), or the 200gm in plastic bag (The Fishmonger)?
[jaygriz] i think because they said 'tinned fish' that they implied its the tinned one.
[AussieDaddy] Good catch. Can't believe I missed that. Cheers

[Charity] Based comment. The Lite version (packed in Indonesia) nothing more Italian than that, is just olive oil, so no seed oils. If you believe that. :)
